socfpga_mbox_client.h

SDM Mailbox hardware abstraction driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Constants
MBOX_WORD_SIZE

Defines the standard 32-bit (4-byte) word size used by the Secure Device Manager (SDM) mailbox FIFO and ARM Trusted Firmware (ATF) payload formatting.

Types
sdm_client_handle

An opaque software handle representing a specific mailbox client. This handle manages the software state, including transaction IDs, callback bindings, and allocated shared memory (DDR) buffers used for asynchronous SDM communication.

mbox_call_back_t

Function signature for the asynchronous response handler. This is executed when the ATF signals (via the S2C ring buffer during polling) that the SDM has completed a specific job and written the response payload into memory.

Parameters
resp_data

A pointer to the populated response data retrieved from the SDM.

Initialization and Teardown
mbox_init
int mbox_init(
void
)

Bootstraps the mailbox client subsystem. This allocates the global client descriptors, initializes synchronization primitives (mutexes/semaphores), and prepares the foundational communication channels with the ARM Trusted Firmware.

Returns

0 on success; a negative error code (e.g., -ENOMEM) if memory allocation fails.

mbox_deinit
int mbox_deinit(
void
)

Tears down the mailbox subsystem. It destroys all active synchronization primitives and releases shared memory buffers back to the bare-metal heap, effectively halting communication with the SDM.

Returns

0 on success; -EIO if internal errors prevent a clean shutdown.

mbox_open_client
sdm_client_handle mbox_open_client(
void
)

Claims an available client descriptor block from the internal pool. This associates the caller with a unique Client ID, which the ATF uses to route asynchronous responses back to the correct software context.

Returns

A valid sdm_client_handle on success; NULL if the maximum number of concurrent clients has been reached.

mbox_close_client
int32_t mbox_close_client(
sdm_client_handle 
mbox_handle
)

Releases a previously allocated client descriptor back to the available pool.  Any pending asynchronous transactions associated with this client ID are effectively orphaned and will be ignored upon SDM completion.

Parameters
mbox_handle
sdm_client_handle

The active client handle to close.

Returns

0 on success; -EIO if the handle is invalid or cannot be closed cleanly.

Note: Prefer mbox_client_acquire / mbox_client_release for bare-metal examples and drivers so they share a single client.

mbox_client_acquire
sdm_client_handle mbox_client_acquire(
void
)

Returns the process-wide shared SDM mailbox client.  On first call, initializes the mailbox subsystem (if needed) and opens one client.  Later calls reuse the same handle.  Intended for single-threaded bare-metal examples/drivers.

Returns

A valid sdm_client_handle on success; NULL on failure.

mbox_client_release
void mbox_client_release(
void
)

Normal example/driver teardown hook.  Does not close the shared client so the next example can reuse it and avoid open/close lifetime issues.

Issues a generic SDM mailbox command through V1 INTEL_SIP_SMC_MBOX_SEND_CMD (synchronous BL31 path). Prefer this over V3 GEN_MBOX, which ATF default-denies for all opcodes except CONFIG_STATUS. Dedicated SiP services (for example FCS) should still use sip_svc_send() with their own function IDs.

Parameters
mbox_handle
sdm_client_handle

The active client handle (validated; V1 sync does not use client/job IDs).

command
uint32_t

The specific SDM mailbox command code.

command_args
uint32_t*

Argument buffer accepted by TF-A is_address_in_ddr_range() (addr >= BL31_LIMIT, typically 0x82000000 on Agilex 5/72), or NULL if none. Stack/BSS buffers below BL31_LIMIT are rejected.

arg_size
uint32_t

The number of bytes in the `command_args` array.

resp
uint32_t*

Response buffer with the same TF-A address rule, or NULL if no payload expected.

resp_size
uint32_t

Capacity of `resp` in bytes.

smc_resp
uint64_t*

Optional: on success [0]=SDM status, [1]=resp words returned.

smc_resp_len
uint32_t

Number of 64-bit entries in `smc_resp`.

Returns

0 on success; -EIO if the command is rejected by the ATF or SDM.

sip_svc_send
int32_t sip_svc_send(
sdm_client_handle 
mbox_handle,
uint64_t 
smc_func_id,
uint64_t 
*
mbox_args,
uint32_t 
arg_len,
uint64_t 
*
resp_data,
uint32_t 
resp_len
)

A lower-level interface to the ARM Trusted Firmware's Silicon Provider (SiP) Service. This function directly formats the provided 64-bit arguments into CPU registers (X1-X7) and invokes the `smc` instruction, bypassing the standard mailbox wrapper for specialized EL3 queries.

Parameters
mbox_handle
sdm_client_handle

The active client handle.

smc_func_id
uint64_t

The 64-bit SMC Function ID (FID) identifying the specific SiP service.

mbox_args
uint64_t*

Pointer to an array of up to 6 arguments to load into X1-X6.

arg_len
uint32_t

The number of arguments provided.

resp_data
uint64_t*

Pointer to a buffer to capture the SMC return registers (X0-X3).

resp_len
uint32_t

The number of return registers to capture.

Returns

0 on success; -EIO if the SMC call fails or returns an error status.

Asynchronous Management
mbox_set_callback
int32_t mbox_set_callback(
sdm_client_handle 
mbox_handle,
mbox_call_back_t 
callback
)

Binds a user-provided asynchronous callback function to the specified client handle. This must be registered before issuing non-blocking mailbox commands, so the polling subsystem knows how to deliver the SDM payload when the transaction finishes.

Parameters
mbox_handle
sdm_client_handle

The active client handle.

callback
mbox_call_back_t

Function pointer to the handler routine.

Returns

0 on success; -EIO if the handle is invalid.

mbox_poll_once
int mbox_poll_once(
void
)

The core asynchronous event pump. This function invokes the `SIP_SMC_GET_TRANS_ID` service to drain the SDM-to-HPS (S2C) ring buffer. For every completed job ID detected, it invokes `SIP_SMC_GET_RESP` to pull the payload from shared memory and fires the registered client callback with the data.

Returns

The number of completed responses processed during this iteration (returns 0 if no new responses were ready).
